d.t: A worded or expressed sentence, phrase, or only a word on its own, which asks for information, a reply, or a response; an interrogative.
A subject or topic for consideration or investigation.
d.e: The question of seniority will be discussed at the meeting.

d.t: A doubt or challenge about the truth, accuracy, or validity of a matter.
d.e: His claim to the property has come under question.

d.t: A proposal to a meeting as a topic for deliberation.
d.e: I move that the question be put to a vote.

d.t: (now archaic, historical, chiefly with definite article) Interrogation by torture.
(obsolete) Talk; conversation; speech.
(transitive) To ask questions of; to interrogate; to ask for information.
(transitive) To raise doubts about; have doubts about.
d.e: He questioned South Korean claims that China is a major source of its pollution.

d.t: (intransitive) To ask a question or questions; inquire or seek to know; examine.
(intransitive, obsolete) To argue; to converse; to dispute.
Moving with speed, rapidity or swiftness, or capable of doing so; rapid; fast.
d.e: I ran to the station – but I wasn't quick enough.

d.t: Occurring in a short time; happening or done rapidly.
Lively, fast-thinking, witty, intelligent.
d.e: You have to be very quick to be able to compete in ad-lib theatrics.

d.t: Mentally agile, alert, perceptive.
d.e: My father is old but he still has a quick wit.

d.t: (of people or tempers) Easily aroused to anger; quick-tempered.
d.e: She has a very quick temper.

d.t: (archaic) Alive, living.
(archaic, of a foetus) At the stage where it can be felt to move in the uterus.
d.e: Whoever does any act under such circumstances that if he thereby caused death he would be guilty of culpable homicide, and does by such act cause the death of a quick unborn child, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to 10 years, and shall also be liable to fine.

d.t: (now rare, archaic) Pregnant, especially at the stage where the foetus's movements can be felt; figuratively, alive with some emotion or feeling.
(archaic, of water) Flowing, not stagnant.
(archaic) Burning, flammable, fiery.
(obsolete) Fresh; bracing; sharp; keen.
(mining, of a vein of ore) productive; not "dead" or barren
Quickly, in a quick manner.
Answer quickly.
Raw or sensitive flesh, especially that underneath finger and toe nails.
Plants used in making a quickset hedge.
The life; the mortal point; a vital part; a part susceptible to serious injury or keen feeling.
(with "the", archaic) Synonym of living (“those who are alive”).
Quitchgrass.
(cricket) A fast bowler.
(transitive) To amalgamate surfaces prior to gilding or silvering by dipping them into a solution of mercury in nitric acid.
(transitive, archaic, poetic) To quicken.
To the greatest extent or degree; completely, entirely.
In a fully justified sense; truly, perfectly, actually.
To a moderate extent or degree; somewhat, rather.
d.e: Mind your shoes, the basement is quite wet.

d.t: (chiefly UK) Indicates agreement; exactly so.
d.e: “That's a rather ugly colour for a house, don't you think?” — “Quite.”

d.t: (bullfighting) A series of passes made with the cape to distract the bull.
